chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from his father Maymoun, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:

To Muhammad bin Suleyman: 'Where have you lodged?' He said, 'In such and such a place.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there anyone with you?' He said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not be alone, move from it, O Maymoun, for Satan is most audacious towards the human being when he is alone.'
ai.seo_question: Why is it recommended to avoid being alone according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) instructs Maymoun ibn Abi Shabib to avoid solitary lodging, highlighting the spiritual vulnerability of the individual. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the psychological and metaphysical impact of isolation, where Satan exploits the lack of divine awareness or companionship to incite fear and sin. The advice underscores the practical importance of maintaining a state of vigilance (yaqzah) even in mundane activities like sleeping.
